name: Aimtron Electronics Ltd
tagline: Small EMS/ODM in a durable China+1 electronics wave with a verified revenue and order-book inflection (FY26 +89%, Q1 FY27 +94%, order book ~2x sales) - but ~72x P/E, negative FY26 operating cash flow and 256 working-capital days make the earnings low-quality at this price
business_overview: EMS / PCB design and assembly company shifting toward ODM / box-build, with defence, AI and IoT exposure and a growing export book; subsidiary Aimtron Mechatronics for a greenfield expansion.
fundamentals_table: P/E ~72x; FY26 CFO negative Rs 40 Cr; debtor days 164, WC days 256; FCF -Rs 87 Cr
fundamentals_narrative: The revenue inflection is validated by actuals: FY26 revenue Rs 301 Cr (+89%), PAT Rs 46 Cr (+79%, EPS Rs 22.31), H2 FY26 revenue Rs 179 Cr accelerating over H1, and the open order book at ~Rs 604 Cr as of 30-Jun-26 (~2x FY26 revenue) with Q1 FY27 revenue +94% YoY. OPM has held ~20% (EBITDA margin 22.6%) - high for box-build EMS, which points to a genuine design-led mix but also carries normalisation risk. Deep-dive pass 1 (2026-09-02): the cash side is the problem - FY26 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE Rs 40 Cr against Rs 61 Cr operating profit, free cash flow -Rs 87 Cr, debtor days 164 and working-capital days 256; the reported profit is entirely absorbed by receivables, inventory and WIP. Borrowings rose to Rs 55 Cr (from Rs 1 Cr) and Rs 94.6 Cr of convertible warrants were raised to fund the Aimtron Mechatronics greenfield and the Jan-2026 acquisition of US-based ICS Inc / AIC (~USD 17M CY25 revenue, target USD 25M in 3 years). No promoter pledge. The stock trades at ~72x FY26 earnings after a ~136% one-year run.
sentiment_summary: No new forum activity since the prior read (thread stable at ~29 live posts, highest #40). Prior steadily-bullish tone stands; most recent post noted the market has caught on and re-rated the stock.
community_signal: No trusted-roster user has posted a conviction call in this thread; Vansh_Dhelia (elevated tier) was the most active and highest-loved poster but without an explicit call.
key_new_facts: Sovrenn lead verified: H2 FY26 sales up ~59-76% YoY to ~Rs 162-179 Cr, PAT up ~71% YoY to ~Rs 24-26 Cr; warrant conversion / preferential raise (~Rs 95 Cr) for greenfield capex.
FY26 revenue Rs 301 Cr (+89%), PAT Rs 46 Cr (+79%); open order book ~Rs 521 Cr (+176% YoY).
bull_case: Verified, still-accelerating growth in a durable China+1 EMS/ODM theme: FY26 revenue +89%, Q1 FY27 +94% YoY, order book ~Rs 604 Cr (~2x FY26 revenue) with AI/IoT/defence/BESS wins
Design-led mix keeps OPM ~20% - well above commodity box-build EMS norms - and ROCE is 28%
US ICS/AIC acquisition adds onshore ESDM/ODM capability and a dollar order book ($9.8M, +36% YoY)
bear_case: FY26 operating cash flow was negative Rs 40 Cr against Rs 46 Cr reported PAT; FCF -Rs 87 Cr, debtor days 164, working-capital days 256 - the earnings are not converting to cash
~72x FY26 P/E after a 136% one-year run - multiple compression is a bigger risk than expansion, and much of the visible order book is already priced
OPM ~20% is high for EMS (Kaynes ~15%, Syrma ~11%); normalisation toward mid-teens would hit the whole thesis
SME-heritage name funding growth with warrants + rising debt; no trusted-roster conviction call in-thread
10x from a ~Rs 3,300 Cr mcap implies becoming Kaynes-sized in 2-3 years off a Rs 301 Cr revenue base - not credible
verdict_headline: Verified growth inflection, but ~72x earnings that do not convert to cash (FY26 CFO -Rs 40 Cr, 256 WC days); thesis_fit cut to neither, conviction to Low-Medium
verdict_reasoning: Deep-dive pass 1 (2026-09-02): the growth is real and continuing - FY26 revenue +89%, Q1 FY27 +94% YoY, order book ~2x FY26 revenue - and the China+1 / defence-electronics theme is durable.

But the deep read surfaces a serious earnings-quality problem: FY26 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE Rs 40 Cr versus Rs 61 Cr operating profit, free cash flow -Rs 87 Cr, working-capital days 256 and debtor days 164. Growth is being funded by Rs 94.6 Cr of convertible warrants plus rising debt (Rs 55 Cr), not by internal accruals.
At ~72x FY26 earnings after a 136% one-year run, the visible order book is largely priced and the dominant risk is multiple compression and/or OPM normalisation from an EMS-high ~20%.

thesis_fit cut from 10x-in-2-3-years to neither: a 10x from Rs 3,300 Cr mcap means becoming Kaynes-sized in 2-3 years off a Rs 301 Cr base - not plausible - and the cash-conversion profile argues against paying up here.
Conviction cut Medium -> Low-Medium: no red flag (no pledge, no regulatory action), but negative operating cash flow at 72x with no trusted-roster corroboration is a Low-Medium, not a Medium.

growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~72x needs sustained 35-45% EPS CAGR AND an elevated exit multiple; the growth rate supports the numerator, but from 72x the dominant move is compression, so treat as priced-in despite the acceleration.
